Root गोम, curadi, meaning उपलेपने. Curadi roots take णिच् → गोमयति. Bhave prayoga uses atmanepada endings, third person singular normally — but here uttama purusha bahuvacana is requested. In bhava prayoga, technically only prathama purusha ekavacana is used; but these exercise sets often just apply the ending mechanically. Actually for karmani/bhave prayoga, the form is passive: यक् + atmanepada endings.

So bhave: गोम् + णिच् → गोमि, then यक् : before यक्, णि is elided? Rule: णेरनिटि (6.4.51) — णि is elided before an ārdhadhātuka affix beginning... actually णेरनिटि: the णि is deleted when a non-iṭ ārdhadhātuka follows. यक् is a vikaraṇa (sārvadhātuka?) — यक् in karmani is added before sārvadhātuka. Hmm, यक् is added in sārvadhātuka contexts (3.1.67 sārvadhātuke yak). So णि is not deleted by णेरनिटि (which requires ārdhadhātuka).

Wait, but for karmani forms of ṇic verbs: चोर्यते. Yes, चुर् + णिच् → चोरि, + यक् → चोर्यते. The इ is deleted by... 6.4.51 णेरनिटि — actually that's applicable to ārdhadhātuka. Hmm. Standard: चोर्यते. The rule is 6.4.51 णेरनिटि: "णि is elided before an affix which is ārdhadhātuka and not beginning with iṭ". But यक् is not ārdhadhātuka. Actually the elision of णि before यक् is by 6.4.51 anyway because... Let's recall: कारि + यते? No, karmani of कारयति is कार्यते. So णि is dropped. The rule used is 6.4.51 णेरनिटि, and यक्... Hmm, some say the lopa is by 6.4.51 treating यक् — actually there's also 6.4.48 अतो लोपः. Wait, कारि → कार्यते: the इ is deleted. Indeed traditional: णेरनिटि applies since यक् ... Actually there's a vārttika. Regardless, form is गोम्यते in karmani/bhave.

Lot, bhave, uttama bahu: ending आमहै (āmahai) for atmanepada lot uttama bahuvacana. Sarvadhatuka lot: उत्तम बहु ātmanepada = महिङ् → आमहै (with आट् augment).

So गोम् + यक् + आमहै = गोम्यामहै.

Check: यक् is य, before आमहै: गोम्य + आमहै → गोम्यामहै. Yes, like पच्यामहै.
</thinking>

<answer>गोम्यामहै</answer>

Root स्पृह, curadi, meaning ईप्सा (desire). Takes णिच्: स्पृह + णिच् → स्पृहयति (no vṛddhi due to... actually स्पृह is a curadi root; laghūpadha guṇa would give स्पर्हयति, but there's a special rule: स्पृहिगृहिपतिदयिनिद्रातन्द्राश्रद्धाभ्य आलुच् — that's for ālu suffix. Actually the standard form is स्पृहयति. The rule is "मीनातिमिनोतीदीपां..." no. There's a vārttika: स्पृहेर्गुणाभावः? Actually Ashtadhyayi 7.3.36... Hmm.

The known form: स्पृहयति (desires), with dative. Yes, स्पृहयति कुसुमाय. So no guṇa of ṛ. Indeed Panini 7.4.29? No. There's a rule "अर्तिह्रीव्लीरीक्नूयीक्ष्माय्यातां पुङ्णौ" no.

Standard: स्पृहयति. So lang: अस्पृहयत्.

With ni-anta, laṅ third singular parasmaipada: अ + स्पृहय + त् = अस्पृहयत्.
</thinking>

<answer>अस्पृहयत्</answer>

Root: वर (curādi, class 10), meaning ईप्सा (desire). Form: वरयति. In bhāva prayoga (impersonal), the verb takes ātmanepada endings with yak (यक्) added — like karmani/bhāve prayoga: वर + णिच् → वरि... Actually bhāve prayoga uses ya (श्यन्-like यक्) after the root: वार्यते? Let's think.

Curādi roots with ṇic: वर + णिच् = वरि (vṛddhi? वर is already... वर → ṇic causes vṛddhi of penultimate 'a'? The a is already... 'अ' vṛddhi is 'आ'. Rule: अत उपधायाः (7.2.116) vṛddhi of upadhā 'a' before ñit/ṇit pratyaya. So वर् → वार्? Hmm, वर: v-a-r-a. The dhātu वर, with ṇic: it's actually "वर" ending in 'a' — like curādi roots ending in vowel? Many curādi roots given as e.g. चुर, चित, etc. In Dhatupatha, चुर is "चुर्" essentially with final 'a' as it-marker? Actually Dhātupāṭha citations like चुरादि: चुर, चित, etc. — the final अ is added for pronunciation. So वर is root वृ? No.

Actually there's dhātu "वर ईप्सायाम्" in curādi. The form is वरयति (like "vara" - to choose/desire). Since it's citation with final अ for utterance, root is वर्. Then ṇic: upadhā is अ, vṛddhi gives वार्? But 7.2.116 अत उपधायाः applies to ṇiti. Hmm, but forms like चुरयति (not चोरयति?) — actually चोरयति with guṇa by pugantalaghūpadhasya... चुर् has उ upadhā laghu → guṇa चोर्. वर् has upadhā अ → vṛddhi आ → वारयति? But known form is वरयति "he chooses"? Hmm, "vṛ" class 9/5 gives vṛṇoti. "vara" desiderative... The verb वरयति (varayati) "chooses, woos" — that's actually from वृ with ṇic: vṛ → vara (vṛddhi? guṇa) + i → varayati. Yes, वरयति is standard: "kanyāṃ varayati". But the Dhātupāṭha curādi entry: "वृ वरणे"? Hmm.

There's curādi entry "वर ईप्सायाम्" — since the root is cited as वर, and forms वरयति. Note 7.2.116 vṛddhi of upadhā अ: but here अ is not upadhā if the root is वर (v-a-r-a) with final अ counted... In dhātupāṭha, roots like कथ, गण, वर, are treated with final अ real? E.g., कथ → कथयति (not काथयति) — because 'a' is final, not upadhā (the 'a' before थ... कथ = k-a-th-a; if final अ is part, then upadhā is अ? Hmm, कथ: sounds k, a, th, a. If final a is real, then the letter before final is थ, and upadhā is अ (the one before थ)? Upadhā = penultimate phoneme = थ? No: phonemes: k, a, th, a. Penultimate = th. So no vṛddhi. Then the final अ is deleted by ato lopaḥ (6.4.48) before णि → कथ्+इ → कथि → कथयति. Yes! That's how curādi roots ending in अ work.

So वर: v,a,r,a. Penultimate = र्, so no vṛddhi. Final अ elided: वर् + इ = वरि → वरयति. Good.

Bhāve prayoga, Lat, madhyama, bahuvacana: with yak (3.1.67 sārvadhātuke yak) and ātmanepada endings. Bhāve prayoga uses only third person singular (ekavacana)! Actually bhāve prayoga is only prathama-puruṣa ekavacana traditionally. But the task asks madhyama bahuvacana — some datasets generate all forms. Form: stem वरि + य + ते. Before yak, ṇi is elided? Rule 6.4.51 ṇer aniṭi: णि is deleted before ārdhadhātuka beginning without iṭ. यक् is sārvadhātuka, so ṇi stays? For karmaṇi: e.g., चोर्यते (coryate) — ṇi is deleted! Because 6.4.51 णेरनिटि applies to ārdhadhātuka... Hmm, actual form: चोर्यते "is stolen". Yes, passives of ṇic verbs drop ṇi: कार्यते? Actually causative passive is कार्यते (kāryate) from kāri + ya → kār-ya-te. The ṇi deletion before yak: rule 6.4.51 ṇer aniṭi deletes ṇi before ārdhadhātuka; yak is not ārdhadhātuka. But there's rule 6.4.51... Hmm, actually the deletion before yak: 6.4.51 is "ṇer aniṭi" — commentary: yak in bhāve/karmaṇi is sārvadhātuka? No — 3.1.67 yak is sārvadhātuka? The yak is a vikaraṇa (sārvadhātuka since it's before tiṅ... actually vikaraṇas are ārdhadhātuka? No, 3.4.113 tiṅśitsārvadhātukam — śit pratyayas are sārvadhātuka. यक् is not śit (य् + अ + क्; it marker is k). So yak is ārdhadhātuka! Wait, 3.1.67 says sārvadhātuke yak — that's the condition (yak comes before sārvadhātuka endings), but yak itself: is it śit? यक् — anubandha क्, not श्. So yak is ārdhadhātuka by 3.4.114 ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣ

Root: लज (curadi, प्रकाशने) — with णिच् → लाजयति (curadi takes णिच्). Bhave prayoga uses atmanepada endings, third person singular normally; but here madhyama purusha eka — bhave prayoga with second person? Bhave prayoga is impersonal, normally prathama purusha ekavacana. But the task asks madhyama eka; conventionally these datasets give the form with आत्मनेपद ending for madhyama ekavacana.

Bhave/karmani: stem = root + यक् (य) + atmanepada endings. With णिच्, the णि is dropped before यक् (णेरनिटि — णि elision before यक्? Actually रुष्यमत्वर... Let's recall: in karmani/bhave, णिच् is elided by "णेरनिटि" (6.4.51) — णि is deleted before आर्धधातुक beginning without इट्. यक् is a सार्वधातुक? No, श्यन्, यक् — यक् (3.1.67) is सार्वधातुक... Actually 6.4.51 णेरनिटि applies before आर्धधातुक. यक् is सार्वधातुक (it's a vikarana for sarvadhatuka lakaras). Hmm, but णि elision before यक्: the rule is 6.4.51 णेरनिटि — "ardhadhatuke" adhikara. So doesn't apply to यक्.

Standard: चोरयति → कर्मणि चोर्यते. Yes! णि is dropped: चुर् + य + ते = चोर्यते. Which rule? 6.4.51 णेरनिटि, with यक् considered... Actually the standard derivation: चुर + णिच् → चोरि; in karmani, यक् added: चोरि + य + ते, and णेरनिटि deletes इ → चोर्यते. It's traditionally accepted (यक् treated as ārdhadhātuka? no). Actually कर्मणि यक् — hmm, but the accepted form is चोर्यते. Yes.

So लज् + णिच् → लाज् (vrddhi of laghu upadha 'a'? अ is already... लज् has अ as upadha; णिच् causes vrddhi: अत उपधायाः? 7.2.116 अत उपधायाः vrddhi in ञ्णिति → लाज्). लाजयति. Karmani/bhave: लाज्यते.

Lot bhave madhyama eka: atmanepada ending थास् → in lot, थास् → स्व (सवाभ्यां वामौ? no). लोट् madhyama eka atmanepada: थास् → स्व (सेर्ह्यपिच्च applies to परस्मैपद सिप्). For atmanepada, थास् in लोट् becomes स्व by 3.4.91? Rule: "थासस्से" (3.4.80) is for लट्... For लोट्: सवाभ्यां वामौ (3.4.91) — no, that's for स-व. Actually थास् → स्व by 3.4.91? Let me recall: एधस्व. यes, लोट् madhyama ekavacana atmanepada = स्व.

So लाज्यस्व.

Check the guna/samprasarana: लाज् + य + स्व = लाज्यस्व.</thinking>

<answer>लाज्यस्व</answer>

Root: दशिँ (daśi) with nasal anubandha ĩ (indicating... actually ि ँ marks it as ñit? No—the "ँ" over the vowel indicates it's anudātta-nasal marker meaning it takes ātmanepada... Actually in Dhatupatha, a nasalized vowel marker (like दशिँ) indicates "ir" ... Let me think: the anunāsika marker on the root's vowel is an indicatory nasal, meaning ... Standard: roots with anunāsika ñ/ṇ etc. Here "दशिँ" — the final इ is an it-marker (ि), and it's nasalized. Curādi roots ending in इ with anunāsika... The nasal marker indicates the root belongs to a class taking ṇic obligatorily (like चुरादि) — actually all curādi take ṇic.

Anyway, root is दंश् ? No — दशि → दश्. Actually "दशिँ" in curādi: दंशिँ? There's a curādi root "दंशँ" ... Let me just use दश् (daś) meaning "to speak" (bhāṣāyām). With ṇic: दश् + णिच् → वृद्धि of अ? अ is already... लघूपधवृद्धि: अ → आ? Actually अत उपधायाः (7.2.116) gives vṛddhi of penultimate अ before ṇit affix: दाश् + इ = दाशि. Hmm, but "अत उपधायाः" applies to ñit/ṇit affixes — यes, णिच् is ṇit. So दाशि.

Wait but for curādi like चुर् → चोरि (guṇa via पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च). For अ-penultimate roots like पठ् (bhvādi) — not relevant. Curādi गण example: कथ् → कथयति (no vṛdhi because... कथ has अ upadhā; कथयति not काथयति). Hmm! Why? Because अत उपधायाः 7.2.116 applies... Actually कथ् is a curādi root कथँ, and it gives कथयति. The rule णौ चङ्युपधायाह्रस्वः applies for caṅ. Hmm.

7.2.116 अत उपधायाः — vṛddhi of अ upadhā before ñit/ṇit pratyaya. This gives पाचि (पाचयति) from पच्. So कथ् should give काथयति? But actual form is कथयति. Because कथ् root is "कथ" already containing the ṇic? No — curādi roots are listed as bases to which ṇic is added obligatorily. कथयति: from कथ + णिच्. Why no vṛddhi? Because of 7.3.34 वा चित्तविरागे? No.

Rule 7.3.36? Actually there's "मितां ह्रस्वः" no. Hmm, there's a rule 7.3.34: "न कपि"? Let me recall: घटादयो मितः (a gaṇasūtra) — roots of ghaṭādi are "mit", and मितां ह्रस्वः (6.4.92) shortens the upadhā before ṇi. But घटादि is in bhvādi.

For कथ्: The vārttika/gaṇasūtra "कथादिभ्यो ण्वुल्..." Hmm. Actually अत उपधायाः applies where? पठ → पाठयति, गम → गमयति (गम is mit). कथ् → कथयति: many say कथ् is ghaṭādi mit? Actually the derivation: कथ is a curādi root, and Kashika notes कथादि are "मित्"? There's gaṇasūtra "कथादयश्च मितः"? Hmm.

Anyway, our root दश् — is it a curādi? Yes, "दशँ/दंशँ भाषायाम्"? There are curādi roots in the list "भाषायाम्" group: e.g., कथ, वद? Actually there is a set of curādi roots with artha भाषायाम्: "कथ, गण? no". Let me recall the curādi list beginning: तक्षँ, रक्षँ ... and there are groups. Roots meaning भाषायाम् in curādi: भाष? Actually curādi contains "कथँ वाक्यप्रबन्धे". Hmm.

Curādi list includes: "वदँ ...". The known set in curādi with भाषायाम्: लपँ? Hmm.

For our answer, likely the stem is दंशयति or दाशयति... Let's decide: the root as given दशिँ — the final इ nasalized. In Dhatupatha, roots like "दशिँ" – the "इ" is an it (indicatory) that shows insertion of nasal (num) — no wait: "अनुदात्तेत् नासिक्य" hmm. Standard convention: roots written with a nasalized vowel like "शुभँ", "इदिँ" — nasalized इ (idit) indicates नुम् insertion (num āgama): इदितो नुम् धातोः (7.1.58). So दशिँ = "daś" with idit → num insertion → दंश्. Wait but दंश् (to bite) is bhvādi as "दंशँ दशने" written दंशँ? Actually the bhvādi root for biting is "दंशँ" listed as दश् with idit? The Dhatupatha entry is "दंशँ दशने" (bhvādi) — hmm, it's typically given as "दशिँ दशने"? Actually yes! Bhvādi root 1.1097? "दंश दशने" — but it's cited as दशिँ with idit, giving दंशति. Hmm, actual: दंश् → दशति (bites) - the present is दशति (num deleted by अनिदिताम् हल उपधायाः क्ङिति... no that's for न loss). दंश् → दशति because of 6.4.24 अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति च — deletes nasal, but that requires the root to be anidit; दंश् must be idit? If idit, nasal retained... Actually दंश्: लट् दशति — nasal lost. Hmm, that's due to 6.

Root: श्रन्थ् (curadi, class 10), meaning सन्दर्भे "stringing together". Curadi roots take णिच् → श्रन्थ् + णिच् → श्रन्थि... Actually curadi with णिच्: श्रन्थ् → वृद्धि? श्रन्थ् has न् as penultimate... laghupadha? The vowel is अ followed by न्थ् — it's a conjunct, so not laghu upadha; also "अत उपधायाः" (7.2.116) requires vṛddhi of अ upadha in ṇiti — that's अत उपधायाः: vṛddhi of penultimate अ before ñit/ṇit. But that applies to अ upadha regardless of conjunct? 7.2.116 अत उपधायाः — vṛddhi of अ in upadha when ñit or ṇit follows. Here upadha of श्रन्थ् is न्... wait, upadha = second-to-last letter. श् र् अ न् थ् — last is थ्, upadha is न्. So no अ upadha. So no vṛddhi. Actually there's also इदितो नुम् — not relevant. Actually श्रन्थ् in curadi: श्रन्थ (सन्दर्भे) — there's a rule ग्रन्थ्, श्रन्थ् etc. There's "श्रन्थ ग्रन्थ" in curadi; forms: श्रन्थयति, ग्रन्थयति.

Hmm, but there's also rule 6.4.24 अनिदितां हल उपधायाः क्ङिति — न् elision, but ṇic is not ङित्. So श्रन्थयति.

Bhave prayoga: impersonal passive, uses yak + atmanepada, always third person singular! But the task asks uttama purusha dvivacana. In bhāve prayoga, strictly only prathama-purusha ekavacana. But these exercise datasets often just generate the form mechanically: passive stem श्रन्थ्यते... Actually with ṇic: the ṇi is dropped before yak (णेरनिटि 6.4.51). So श्रन्थ् + य + ते → श्रन्थ्यते. Uttama dvivacana: श्रन्थ्यावहे.

Wait — ṇic dropped: श्रन्थ् + य = श्रन्थ्य. Uttama dvi ātmanepada Lat: वहि → आवहि → आवहे. So श्रन्थ्यावहे.

Hmm, but does the root undergo any change? No.

Answer: श्रन्थ्यावहे.</thinking><answer>श्रन्थ्यावहे</answer>

Root: श्वभ्र् (curadi, class 10), with ṇic. Bhāve prayoga — impersonal, always ātmanepada, and takes third person singular normally. But the task asks for second person plural in bhāve prayoga — conventionally these paradigms are generated mechanically: bhāva/karmaṇi prayoga uses ātmanepada endings with the ya-vikaraṇa (present system) but āśīrliṅ karmaṇi/bhāve uses the sīyuṭ ātmanepada precative endings on the root (not the ya).

Actually, in karmaṇi/bhāve āśīrliṅ, the form is like liṅ ātmanepada: e.g., √kṛ → kriyeta? No—āśīrliṅ ātmanepada: kṛṣīṣṭa. Karmaṇi āśīrliṅ: kriyeta? Let's recall: karmaṇi prayoga in ārdhadhātuka lakāras uses the root with ātmanepada endings (no yak, except in luṅ/liṅ? ). Rule: yak is added in sārvadhātuka (3.1.67 sārvadhātuke yak). Āśīrliṅ is ārdhadhātuka, so no yak. So karmaṇi āśīrliṅ = ātmanepada precative endings, with cin-vad rules for ciṇ... Actually for karmaṇi āśīrliṅ there's special: "ciṇ-vad bhāve karmaṇi" — 6.4.62: syasicsīyuṭtāsiṣu bhāvakarmaṇoḥ upadeśe'jjhanagrahadṛśāṃ vā ciṇvad iṭ ca.
